subject.title: [Feature]: WebUI notification system, cron job management popups, and context monitor integration

question: Should OpenClaw define a shared connected-Control-UI notification/action queue for cron results and context pressure, and should cron snooze/reschedule mutate existing jobs or create one-shot follow-up jobs?
rationale: The missing behavior is real, but the durable boundary crosses Control UI notification architecture, cron scheduling semantics, context-pressure UX, Web Push overlap, and WebChat action-contract work.

options.title: Design Shared UI Notifications First
options.body: Add one Control UI notification/action contract and then implement cron-result and context-pressure actions on top of it.

options.title: Fold Into WebChat Actions
options.body: Treat cron/context notifications as another client action surface under the broader WebChat presentation and callback contract.

options.title: Defer In-App Popups
options.body: Keep existing inline context warnings, cron history, and Web Push settings while leaving actionable popups for a later roadmap decision.

recommendation.title: Design Shared UI Notifications First
recommendation.body: Add one Control UI notification/action contract and then implement cron-result and context-pressure actions on top of it.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest combined history signal across cron gateway behavior, notification delivery, and the prior product review context.
